releases.notes:
**Unofficial** Anubis 1.0 build from `anubis-modded` (commit 4678e54). GPL-3.0-only. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the original author.

- `anubis-1.0+mc1.21.11-sound-detectors.jar`, SHA-256 `3366e0a664e82a15ce3ae08933b21e1d0cf95c7f205bd0ccfe6e0ee861da0c4e`
- Needs Fabric Loader 0.16+ and Fabric API. Litematica is optional.

**Changes since v1.0-donut-sound**

- **Donut Sound Detector** (Base Finding) is now its own module. It is the one-to-one port of the Sound Detector from [Donut Client 3.0](https://github.com/Raindots/donut-client) (MIT), with every Donut indicator, warning card, chime, chat notice, world marker, rule, expected area, server profile, history and settings screen. Its preferences are saved to `config/anubis/donut-sound-detector.json`.
- **Sound Detector** (Base Finding) is back as it was in v1.0-basefinder-tools. It marks containers, workstations, doors, mining, building and player sounds heard with nobody in sight, and keeps its history panel, snooze and copper golem filter.
- The two modules don't share settings and can run at the same time.

**Tested** on a local Paper + ChunkVeil server with both modules on:

- Both alerted independently on chests, barrels, the anvil, grindstone, smithing and enchanting tables, the chiseled bookshelf and the decorated pot.
- Only the Sound Detector alerted on doors, switches, block placing, attacks and eating, because Donut scores those below its warning threshold.

Not yet tested on DonutSMP.

The `main` branch is the plain decompiled Anubis source. All the added modules live on `anubis-modded`.

mods.description: Anubis is a standalone client utility mod focused on overlays, quality-of-life tooling, and advanced visual debugging.

releases.notes:
**Unofficial** Anubis 1.0 build from `anubis-modded` (commit 0738faf). GPL-3.0-only. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the original author.

- `anubis-1.0+mc1.21.11-donut-sound.jar`, SHA-256 `7b4d9bfb6bc762ebb05f17c2b6456646cc5b8f7ec5a8627d6981752e0f4e20bd`
- Needs Fabric Loader 0.16+ and Fabric API. Litematica is optional.

**What changed since v1.0-basefinder-tools**

**Sound Detector** (Base Finding) is now a one-to-one port of the Sound Detector from [Donut Client 3.0](https://github.com/Raindots/donut-client) (MIT; its notice ships as `licenses/donut-client-MIT.txt`). The port includes all of these Donut features:

- **Capture:** sound, entity sound, block event, world event, mining progress, entity status, damage, explosion and stop-sound packets. It also captures client-side sounds, and tracks your own actions so it can filter them out.
- **Classification:** it classifies against all 1,791 vanilla sound events and every block's material sounds, using 14 categories.
- **Scoring:** it scores activity into warning and critical incidents.
- **Presets:** Balanced activity, Players only, Base activity and Diagnostics.
- **Filtering:** custom rules (wildcards, block tags, condition groups), expected areas, trusted players, and per-server profiles.
- **Alerts:** warning cards, a chime, chat notices and world markers.
- **History and screens:**
  - an activity history with an evidence inspector
  - acknowledge, snooze and mute, with keybinds
  - a full settings screen and a draggable card preview
  - JSON import/export and a block/sound coverage export

Every Donut indicator is included, even ones some anti-xray plugins block. ChunkVeil cancels positional sounds inside its hidden zone by default, so on a server like that only activity above or outside the masked layer comes through.

The module's settings mirror Donut's main settings page. *All Appearance, Audio And Behavior Controls* opens every preference. Preferences are saved to `config/anubis/sound-detector.json`. Base Finder keeps its own sound evidence.

**Tested:**
- Donut's 28 Sound Engine unit tests pass against the port.
- On a local Paper + ChunkVeil server, sounds played near the player raised the warnings Donut gives: containers, the anvil, grindstone, smithing and enchanting tables, chiseled bookshelf, decorated pot, and explosions.
- Doors, switches, building and machinery scored under the warning threshold, as in Donut, so they only show in history.
- Mob and ambient sounds were ignored.

Not yet tested on DonutSMP.

releases.notes:
**Unofficial** Anubis 1.0 build from `anubis-modded` (commit 53b2fcb). GPL-3.0-only. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the original author.

- `anubis-1.0+mc1.21.11-basefinder-tools.jar` — SHA-256 `20d68f22540d5615b16bf31cb7852747cb2f0569bb4ea3560ba8f8f315521b47`
- Needs Fabric Loader 0.16+ and Fabric API. Litematica is optional.

**Modules added on top of Anubis 1.0**

- **Base Finder** (Base Finding): ranks loaded chunks by how likely they hide a base and shows why.
- **Seed Block ESP** (Render): seeded xray. Runs Minecraft's own world generator for the seed (ported from [Donut Client](https://github.com/NotRaindoots/donut-client), MIT) and boxes ores where they were generated, including under anti-xray's fake deepslate. Overworld ores (stone/deepslate filters) and, in the Nether, ancient debris (netherite), Nether gold and quartz. Checks the seed against ores you can see. Local tests: 297/300 positions correct, 453/453 ores in a full chunk, 3/3 ancient debris in a Nether chunk.
- **Sound Detector** (Base Finding): marks containers, workstations, doors/trapdoors/gates/levers/buttons, mining, building and player sounds (including footsteps) heard with nobody visible nearby. Opt-in *Base activity* for running machinery. Ignores chests next to copper golems. Chat alerts with optional chime, history panel, per-area snooze.
- **Hidden Player ESP** (Base Finding): boxes entities whose position the server leaks without ever spawning them; red when moving at player speed, amber for snapshot positions (e.g. after relogging).
- **Leak Test** (Base Finding): diagnostic that logs what a server still sends from inside its hidden underground and about hidden entities, to `config/anubis/leak-test.log`.

Not yet tested on DonutSMP. See the README for details and test results.

releases.notes:
**Unofficial** Anubis 1.0 with the added **Base Finder** module (Base Finding category), built from `anubis-modded`. GPL-3.0-only. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the original author.

- `anubis-1.0+mc1.21.11-basefinder.jar` — built from commit 654975a
  SHA-256 `fb898a0f3c4b8d7eb73038230f75504bdae77c5493b217561f363ae0a18944b4`
- Needs Fabric Loader 0.16+ and Fabric API. Litematica is optional.

Base Finder ranks loaded chunks by how likely they hide a base and shows why (panel, dots, tooltips). Signals: buried storage and crafted blocks, rotated deepslate, hand-mined tunnels/shafts/rooms, surface builds, signs/banners/heads, lit portals, buried farms, item frames/armor stands, pets and animal farms, grown amethyst/kelp, players seen underground, and hidden players (out-of-sight digging, chest/door use, Player Bypass's ticking-chunk inference). Recognises servers that hide the underground as flat deepslate (DonutSMP-style). New in this build: an opt-in *Hidden Lights (Light Leaks)* setting that reads the light data such servers may still send; it is off by default because natural light sources also trigger it. See the README for the full signal list and what was tested.

releases.notes:
**Unofficial** modded build of Anubis 0.9.9.1 by **4ldenz**, from the `anubis-modded` branch. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the original author. GPL-3.0-only.

> **Pre-release:** the new Base Finder compiles and builds, but hasn't been tested in-game yet. Detection thresholds may need tuning.

## What's new: Base Finder
A new module in the **Base Finding** category. It combines several signals into one ranked list:
- Players hiding underground (live, remembered for a configurable time)
- Player storage, crafted blocks, redstone, placed lights and building blocks buried below the surface
- Rotated deepslate, which natural generation never produces
- Hand-mined tunnels (straight 1x2) and shafts (1x1), deep underground
- Grown amethyst and kelp, plus long dripstone, which only grow while players keep a chunk loaded
- False positives from strongholds, ancient cities, trial chambers, dungeons, ruined portals and monuments are suppressed

Flagged chunks get a soft tile at the depth of the evidence and a dot. Aim at the dot to see why it was flagged. A top-left panel ranks the most likely chunks with distance and direction.

Original implementation; no code from Prestige or the Glazed addon.

## Requirements
- Minecraft **1.21.11**, Fabric Loader **0.16.0+**, **Fabric API**
